title: String literals, escape sequences and special characters
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its output.

understand.concept: String literals use double quotes and include a terminating null character. Escape sequences represent characters such as newline, tab, quotes and backslashes.
understand.whyItMatters: This concept supports correct handling of C data and helps prevent invalid memory access or incorrect program behaviour.
understand.analogy: Think of the construct as a precisely bounded sequence of storage and operations.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's rules for object lifetime, bounds, types or undefined behaviour.

explain.narrative:
String literals use double quotes and include a terminating null character. Escape sequences represent characters such as newline, tab, quotes and backslashes.

Always check the types, object bounds and preconditions required by the operation. Compile with warnings enabled and test ordinary as well as boundary inputs.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Escape sequences change the actual characters represented in the string; they are not merely visual decoration in source code.

practise.guidedTask: The tab escape separates the label from Ada, newline starts a new output line, and escaped quotes appear as quote characters.
practise.independentTask: Identify each escape sequence and predict the number of output lines.
hints: Print a two-line receipt with a tab-separated item and a quoted message.
Adjacent string literals are concatenated during translation.
The character constant '\0' is a null character; the string literal "\0" also has its own final terminator.
